clue.text: Large spruce

definitions.meaning: second meaning: neat and in good order

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a big conifer; both words are separate meanings of one short adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a sizeable one, and a spruce, well-kept room is orderly and neat.

clue.text: Everyone playing occasionally taunts twit

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, every other one from taunts twit

explanation.surface: Someone now and then taunts a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of taunts twit are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction for all performers in an orchestra to play together.

clue.text: Odd clanks affected area of London

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange clanking noises disturbing a part of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Docklands is the redeveloped former port district in east London, around Canary Wharf.

clue.text: Rally around crook in charge, like some American politicians

parts.note: a demo is a protest rally
C is short for circa, Latin for around
a rat is a scoundrel or crook

explanation.surface: A political rally gathers round a corrupt figure in charge, the sort of scene from a US party convention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment signal but here simply gives C, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the US Democratic Party are described by this adjective, one of the two major parties.

clue.text: In which partner takes steps to leave you?

definitions.text: In which partner takes steps to leave you?

parts.words: In which partner takes steps to leave you
parts.note: a dance where another dancer cuts in and your partner moves off with them

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a relationship breaking up; the steps are dance steps, and the phrase is how someone politely cuts in.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse-me is a ballroom dance in which people may claim someone else's partner.

clue.text: Bad loser packing in golf — people staring

indicators.note: packing in means holding something inside, so one piece is placed within
bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of loser are rearranged

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sore loser quits golf while onlookers stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing in' looks like quitting; here it puts G inside OLERS, the anagram of LOSER.
explanation.definitionFit: Oglers are those who leer or look intently at someone, often rudely.

clue.text: Sadly, never once meet again

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of never once are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wistful regret about a reunion that never happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble or gather once more after a break.

clue.text: Part of saw's also extremely tough

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters of tough

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A remark that a saw is also really tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth is one of the sharp points along a saw blade's cutting edge.

clue.text: Woodworking, find fault with door?

parts.note: to carp is to complain or nitpick
a door is an entry, a way in

explanation.surface: Complaining about a badly made door in a woodwork shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the craft of making and fixing wooden structures, a joiner's trade.

clue.text: Spite of ambassador cancelling ball

indicators.note: cancelling means wiping something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic representative, like an ambassador
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: An ambassador spitefully calls off a diplomatic ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful jealousy, close to malice or ill will.

clue.text: Specialist caught in China let off

indicators.note: in signals that the C sits inside the rearranged letters
off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of China let are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricketing expert notes a catch dropped by a player called China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside the anagram of CHINALET (signalled by 'off').
explanation.definitionFit: Technical language or knowledge is specialised, belonging to an expert field.

clue.text: Singing group's papers picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for papers is taken by its sound

parts.note: a quire is a set of sheets of paper, traditionally 24 or 25

explanation.surface: A singing group's sheet music has been gathered up off the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIRE and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a body of singers performing together, often in a church.

clue.text: Independent butcher somewhere in the Hebrides

parts.note: to butcher is to slay or slaughter

explanation.surface: A village butcher who runs his own shop out on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are the islands off Scotland's west coast; Islay is famous for whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is one of the Inner Hebridean islands, so it is a place in that archipelago.

clue.text: Band securing locks in small bar

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a Crunchie is a British honeycomb chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Something holding locks secure inside a little bar, as if a door fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: A Crunchie is a chocolate bar made by Cadbury in Britain; 'locks' are hair, not door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrunchie is a fabric-covered elastic hair tie that holds a ponytail in place.

clue.text: French officer spread marge, eating leftover

indicators.note: eating means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other
spread here means scattered about, so the letters of marge are rearranged

parts.note: an end is a remnant or leftover piece, like a candle end

explanation.surface: A Frenchman spreading margarine on toast while finishing up leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts END inside GARME, the anagram of MARGE signalled by 'spread'; 'spread' and 'marge' both suggest butter substitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French police force, a paramilitary officer of law.

clue.text: Shun support and leave Six Nations team short on energy

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter

parts.note: Italy is one of the six teams in rugby union's Six Nations championship
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rugby player quitting the Italian side, running low on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Six Nations is the annual European rugby union tournament; Italy shortened loses Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is to act independently, refusing help or backing from others.

clue.text: In the morning, man starts to nod off after a coffee

indicators.note: after puts the starting letters of nod off behind A

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, before noon
Eric is a man's name

indicators.note: starts means only the first letter of each of nod and off

parts.note: first letter of nod
first letter of off

explanation.surface: A man dozes off in the morning after drinking a coffee, which oddly failed to wake him.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is espresso diluted with hot water, a common café drink.

clue.text: Floor's regularly dirty in cheap accommodation

parts.note: a floor such as the sea floor is a bed, so floors are beds

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of dirty

parts.note: its second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A grimy floor in a cheap rented room.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Floor's as plural floors, the sea floor sense: beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room for sleeping and living, typically low-cost British lodging.

clue.text: Victim of the drink lying on bed?

definitions.text: Victim of the drink lying on bed?

parts.words: Victim of the drink lying on bed
parts.note: the drink is the sea, and the bed is the seabed where a sunken vessel lies

explanation.walkthrough: It paints a drunk passed out on a bed; 'the drink' is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecked ship is a casualty of the sea, resting on the ocean floor.

clue.text: Tie essential for Oxford but not Wellington

definitions.text: Tie essential for Oxford but not Wellington

parts.words: Tie essential for Oxford but not Wellington
parts.note: an Oxford is a laced shoe, a Wellington is a pull-on rubber boot

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford and Wellington sound like a university and a public school, or a duke; they are footwear, and the tie is a lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoelace is the cord tying up a laced shoe; wellington boots, rubber rain boots, need none.

clue.text: Published new version of Susie Dent's preface

indicators.note: a new version reworks the name Susie, so its letters are rearranged
the preface is the opening, so only the first letter of Dent's is taken

parts.note: first letter of Dent's

explanation.surface: A dictionary expert's foreword appears in a revised edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Susie Dent is the lexicographer on the British TV word show Countdown. The anagram of SUSIE gives ISSUE, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book is to put it out to the public, the same as publishing it.

clue.text: Might Cheshire Cat grin so insincerely?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Cheshire is a cheese, and a cheesy grin is a broad forced smile
second meaning: in a corny, false manner

explanation.walkthrough: The Cheshire Cat from Alice in Wonderland is famous for its grin; Cheshire is also an English cheese, so its grin would be cheesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy means corny or false, so doing something in that way is doing it without sincerity.

clue.text: Kind chap in cast

indicators.note: in means the man piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cast is a tinge of colour, a hue
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A generous fellow among the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors in a play, but here it means a tint.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate and merciful toward others, showing goodness.

clue.text: Credit note

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to ascribe something to someone
second meaning, a noun: a characteristic quality

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a credit note from a shop; the two words are separate senses with different stresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute a quote is to ascribe it to someone; an attribute is a distinguishing feature or characteristic.

clue.text: Reportedly drops Banks

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: tears are drops falling from the eyes

explanation.surface: A news report that banks are dropping, perhaps interest rates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are rows or layers placed one above another, like banks of seats.

clue.text: Muslim leader in Cuba wandering around

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the letters are read backwards
in means the letters sit inside the words Cuba wandering

explanation.surface: An Islamic leader roams around Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: BAWAN runs across the end of Cuba and the start of wandering; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim governor or prince in Mughal India, a title of rank.

clue.text: Alliance senator embraces

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the letters are inside senator

explanation.surface: A politician welcomes a military alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a defence pact of Western nations.

clue.text: Bar put no filling in tatty sandwich

parts.note: bar can mean but, as in all bar one

indicators.note: no filling means the middle is gone, leaving the outer letters of tatty

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pub serves a shabby sandwich with nothing inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is a northern British word for a sandwich, as in chip butty.
explanation.definitionFit: A butty is an informal British term for a filled bread roll or slice.

clue.text: Love neat last letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
mega is slang for great, excellent, or neat

explanation.surface: A tidy, loving signature at the end of a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' means a character of the alphabet, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Quarters? A unit soldiers finally get

parts.note: a part is a component or unit of something
men is a common word for soldiers

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of get is used

parts.note: last letter of get

explanation.surface: A military unit is allocated quarters at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' means lodgings, not fourths.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a set of rooms to live in, the same as living quarters.

clue.text: Doctor donates fee for book

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician gives away his fee to fund a book.
explanation.definitionFit: East of Eden is John Steinbeck's 1952 novel, so it is a well-known title.

clue.text: Fine wine, unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter is removed, as a bottle with no top

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: A wine is judged good although the bottle stays unopened.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the opening T from TOKAY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means acceptable or all right, a casual synonym for fine.
